title: Impact of Additional Representative on Public Spending

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).  

Why: The second representative is assigned deterministically when district population crosses an ex-ante threshold. Near that cutoff, districts just above and just below the threshold should be comparable, so the discontinuity in treatment status can be exploited for causal inference.  

Key assumptions  
• Sharp RDD: Treated = 1 if and only if population ≥ cutoff (≈0.50 after normalisation).  
• Continuity: Potential outcomes (public spending per capita) would have evolved smoothly in the running variable’s absence of treatment. Any jump at the cutoff is therefore attributable to the extra representative.  
• No precise manipulation: Districts cannot finely sort their population to just above the threshold (checked with a McCrary density test).  

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Impact of an Additional Representative on Public Spending
# File path: experiments/exp_b/data/s99_data.csv
############################################################

# 0. Packages ------------------------------------------------
required <- c("tidyverse", "rdrobust", "rddensity")
installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
for(p in required[!required %in% installed]) install.packages(p, quiet = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(rdrobust)   # for rdrobust and rdplot
library(rddensity)  # McCrary density test

# 1. Read data ----------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s99_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 running_var = col_double(),
                 treated     = col_integer(),
                 y           = col_double(),
                 near_cutoff = col_integer()
               ))

# 2. Basic RDD estimation -----------------------------------
cutoff <- 0.5   # inferred threshold
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff)

cat("\n=== Main RDD Estimate (local-linear, MSE-optimal h) ===\n")
print(rd_main$coef[1])     # point estimate
print(rd_main$se[1])       # standard error

# 3. Graphical inspection -----------------------------------
# (Uncomment next 3 lines to display plot in interactive use)
# rdplot(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff,
#        x.label = "Normalised population (running var)",
#        y.label = "Public spending per capita")

# 4. Robustness checks --------------------------------------

## 4a. Different bandwidths
bw_10 <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = 0.10)
bw_20 <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = 0.20)

cat("\n--- Robustness: Different ad-hoc bandwidths ---\n")
out_bw <- tibble(
  Bandwidth = c(0.10, 0.20, rd_main$bws[1]),
  Estimate  = c(bw_10$coef[1], bw_20$coef[1], rd_main$coef[1]),
  SE        = c(bw_10$se[1],   bw_20$se[1],   rd_main$se[1])
)
print(out_bw)

## 4b. Higher-order polynomial
rd_quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2)
cat("\n--- Robustness: Quadratic specification ---\n")
print(rd_quad$coef[1])
print(rd_quad$se[1])

## 4c. Placebo cutoff
placebo_cut <- 0.3
rd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = placebo_cut)
cat("\n--- Placebo cutoff at 0.30 (should be ~0) ---\n")
print(rd_placebo$coef[1])
print(rd_placebo$se[1])

## 4d. McCrary density test
dens <- rddensity(X = df$running_var, c = cutoff)
cat("\n--- McCrary density test (no manipulation if p-value > .05) ---\n")
print(dens$test)

# 5. Clean numeric output for replication -------------------
cat("\n******** Key Result ********\n")
cat("Local average treatment effect at cutoff: ",
    round(rd_main$coef[1], 4),
    " (SE = ", round(rd_main$se[1], 4), ")\n", sep = "")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Districts just above the population threshold receive a second representative who can lobby for their constituency, so per-capita public spending should jump upward at the cutoff.  

Magnitude: Given y is normalised to roughly 0–1, a discontinuity of about +0.15 (15 percentage-points of the outcome’s scale) seems plausible. This would be sizable yet not implausibly large relative to the observed variance.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the population threshold for a second representative as a cutoff for treatment assignment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The presence of a second representative decreases public spending per capita.
